title: Separate output from errors
goal: Observe streams, truncation and pipeline exit status before trusting a report.
challenge: Copy supplied input using stdin/stdout redirects. Demonstrate an input failure truncating a disposable output, retain stderr, compare default and pipefail statuses, and use tee. Explain why a pipeline can report success while an earlier command failed.

steps.explanation: Create a unique learner-owned guest workspace. Stop if creation or cd fails. Retain its printed path; variables do not survive disk Resume.
steps.expected: A fresh directory inside the guest home; no existing files are changed.

steps.command: printf '%s\n' alpha beta > input.txt; printf '%s\n' retained > empty.txt
steps.explanation: Only this disposable output will be used to demonstrate truncation.
steps.expected: Two input lines and an initial output.

steps.command: cat < input.txt > copy.txt; cat missing.txt > empty.txt 2> errors.txt; failed=$?; printf 'failed=%s\n' "$failed" > status.txt
steps.explanation: The shell opens/truncates > before cat tries to read. A failed command does not restore the old output.
steps.expected: copy matches input; empty.txt is empty; stderr and status 1 retained.

steps.command: set +o pipefail; cat missing.txt 2> pipe-errors.txt | wc -l > count.txt; printf 'default=%s\n' "$?" >> status.txt
steps.explanation: Without pipefail the pipeline status is the last command status; wc can succeed on no input.
steps.expected: count is 0; default status 0, despite stderr.

steps.command: set -o pipefail; cat missing.txt 2>> pipe-errors.txt | wc -l > count.txt; printf 'pipefail=%s\n' "$?" >> status.txt; set +o pipefail
steps.explanation: With pipefail this pipeline reports its rightmost nonzero status. Restore the practice-shell setting after the comparison.
steps.expected: pipefail status 1; count is still 0, errors remain.

steps.command: printf '%s\n' observed | tee observed.txt; cat status.txt; cmp input.txt copy.txt
steps.explanation: tee writes stdout and a named file. Check status and artifacts separately.

hints: Does pipefail prevent truncation or roll back partial output?
Compare actual output, immediate exit status and resulting files. A syntactically valid command or script can still do the wrong thing.
Keep the original, verify a small intended change, and demonstrate rollback inside this workspace.
review: I retained the stated observations and can explain the outcome.
I checked failure cases and preserved originals; my review is not an application-verified score.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 partial 103.4, 105.2 status preparation. Reinforcement is labeled; no full-objective mastery. Completion records self-review, not verified assessment. No score.
